newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes touch firmer buoyed by palladium.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes touch firmer buoyed by palladium.

text.p: The gold lifted off early depressed levels by Thursday afternoon as buying returned to palladium and helped restore morale somewhat across the precious metals complex, dealers said.
Earlier prices reflected the impact of news on Wednesday that Switzerland planned to liquidate some bullion holdings.
Gold fixed at $353.10 per ounce almost a dollar up from the morning's $2.35 lower.
Comex prices were a little firmer too with the April contract showing a $0.40 gain at $354.80 after opening lower.
Switzerland's president on Wednesday proposed a transfer of revalued bullion reserves to a foundation to assist victims of the Holocaust and other tragedies.
Volume was fairly low in Europe but dealers noted trade buying had come into palladium and encouraged further interest in the rest, although gold was probably the lightest beneficiary.
So far on Thursday spot gold bids have held to a narrow range of $353.30-$351.40 after touching $350.65 on Wednesday.

Prices had already slipped from a peak of $364 two days before the news from Switzerland hit the market and some analysts thought gold may be settling back into a downtrend that saw it fix at a 3-3/4 year low of 336.90 on February 12.

The estimated 40 tonnes of gold to be sold by the Swiss humanitarian foundation over 10 years could be absorbed by the market, but the announcement raised the spectre of other central banks liquidating bullion.

"I know the people from the central bank and they should be able to do it without affecting the market, that's why I am not worried about the actual sale," said analyst Hanspeter Hausheer of Swiss Bank Corp.
"It's the psychological affect...one central bank doesn't do something like this without discussing it with other banks," he added.
Analyst Andy Smith of Union Bank of Switzerland said prices were unlikely to soon recover from the shock.
"The gold price was $357 on the announcement by the Swiss National Bank; remember it well, it may be a long time coming round again," he said.
Silver was about three cents firmer at $5.21/$5.23 per ounce and attempting to stabilise, analysts said.
Solid support was pegged at $5.15, they added.
Platinum recovered from early professional selling to be $3.00 firmer at $384.00/$385.00 per ounce. A firm floor was seen at $375, dealers said.
Palladium recovered on trade buying from Wednesday's low at $142.25 and was quoted $7.75 firmer at $150.00/$151.00.
